intro: A clearer way to route your traffic. RouteLoom is building one self-hosted proxy experience for your desktop, phone, and cloud server.
notice: Pre-alpha. No public app downloads yet.
panelCaption: Illustrative rule preview · no traffic is sent
sampleTitle: A small rule. A clear decision.
sampleText: Choose an example to see how a routing policy could work. This demo runs only in your browser.
sampleResults: PROXY — the default server route matches.
BLOCK — the explicit domain rule matches.
howIntro: A simple connection flow is the destination. Here is what we’re building.
steps: Run your own server with a guided setup and clear upgrade paths.
Add a device using a short-lived invitation. Manage access per device.
Choose direct, proxy, or block rules, then inspect why a route matched.
platformIntro: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS/iPadOS are all in the first-release scope. Capabilities will respect each operating system.
appleNote: Apple platforms have additional routing, entitlement, signing, and distribution constraints. Per-app VPN on iOS requires managed devices.
roadmapIntro: Follow implementation as it happens. Each milestone is a release gate, not a promise of an available feature.
milestones: Shared policy engine, bilingual interface, website, and build checks.
Authenticated transport, server setup, device enrollment, and native adapters.
Routing, UDP, DNS, supported PAC integration, and diagnostics on all five platforms.
Device testing, security review, signing, upgrades, and bilingual documentation.
footerText: Read the source, follow development, or help shape the first release.
footerNote: Apache-2.0 · English & 简体中文 · Self-hosted by design
docsIntro: This is a developer preview. It does not proxy or capture network traffic yet.
docsSections: The Rust policy engine evaluates ordered domain, CIDR, port, and protocol rules. The CLI validates and explains policies. The client interface is bilingual. The server scaffold exposes only local health information.
Install the Rust toolchain specified in rust-toolchain.toml, then run these commands from the repository root.
Install the pinned Flutter SDK, generate the native runners, and run the interface on a supported development machine. Native VPN adapters are still pending.
Cloud-server deployment will begin after authentication, TLS, enrollment, and outbound-access controls are implemented and tested. Do not expose the health scaffold as a public proxy.

Choose an item in the roadmap. Include tests for routing and security behavior, and update both languages when changing visible text. No paid account or cloud server is needed for policy-engine development.
